name: AIPAC
summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee, a pro-Israel lobby founded in 1954 and long counted among the most influential in Washington. Since 2022 it has spent on elections through its own PAC and its super PAC, the United Democracy Project, mostly against candidates (largely Democrats, but also Republican Thomas Massie) it considers insufficiently supportive of Israel. Critics say it aligns closely with right-wing Israeli governments; it calls itself bipartisan.

finances.description: United Democracy Project; $26.1M on independent expenditures in Democratic House races.
United Democracy Project; $34.8M on independent expenditures.

connections.name: Paul Singer
connections.description: Gave $5.6 million to its super PAC, the United Democracy Project, from 2022 to 2026, including $2.6 million in the 2026 cycle. FEC filings show $5,600,000 from Paul Singer to United Democracy Project ('UDP') in 3 cycles (2022–2026).

sources.title: AIPAC's network has already spent $67.2 million to shape the midterm elections — Truthout
FEC receipts: SINGER, PAUL to United Democracy Project ('UDP')

connections.name: Thomas Massie
connections.description: Its super PAC, the United Democracy Project, spent about $4.1 million (estimates range from $2.6 million to $5 million) mostly on attack ads against Massie in Kentucky's May 2026 Republican primary, the most expensive House primary on record; Massie lost to Trump-backed Ed Gallrein.

connections.name: Bernie Sanders
connections.description: In 2020 Sanders said AIPAC provides a platform for bigotry and opposition to Palestinian rights, and refused to attend its conference.

connections.name: Zohran Mamdani
connections.description: In 2025 the National Black Empowerment Action Fund said it would spend $1.3 million against the DSA agenda in New York's mayoral race. Wikipedia says AIPAC helped fund the group; news reports reviewed confirm only that its founder, Darius Jones, is an AIPAC alumnus.

connections.description: Netanyahu has addressed its policy conferences in person and by satellite.

connections.name: Abdul El-Sayed
connections.description: AIPAC and affiliated groups spent close to $30 million backing Rep. Haley Stevens against him in Michigan's 2026 Senate primary, their largest investment in a single race; he won narrowly.
